models_evaluated: 28 state-of-the-art LLMs (proprietary, general-purpose open-source, and medical open-source; specific names not given in text)

links.outcome: LLM accuracy on board questions after adding irrelevant distractor statements
links.effect: Accuracy was reduced by as much as 20.4% with distractors; 1 model that had previously passed failed. Open-source models declined more than proprietary ones.
links.quote: When exposed to distractions, accuracy across various model architectures was significantly reduced-by as much as 20.4%-with 1 model failing that had previously passed.

links.outcome: Whether exam-style benchmark performance reflects robustness in realistic clinical text
links.effect: 6 of 28 LLMs passed the board threshold, but performance was markedly vulnerable to extraneous distracting information.
links.quote: While current LLMs demonstrate an impressive ability to answer neurosurgery board-like examination questions, their performance is markedly vulnerable to extraneous, distracting information.

screen.reason: Empirical benchmark evaluating LLM performance and fragility/robustness to distractor sentences on neurosurgery board exam questions without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment practice.
